newsitem.title: UK: Options - Coffee vols off despite onset of frost season.
newsitem.headline: Options - Coffee vols off despite onset of frost season.

text.p: Volatilities in LIFFE July coffee options have fallen to historically cheap levels this week despite the approaching Brazilian frost season, traders said on Thursday.
The May options saw brisk book-squaring activity ahead of the contract's expiry on April 16.
The May volatilities are now irrelevant and traders said the contract should go off the board without any fireworks as there were no large open positions.
In cocoa, buying interest centred on July calls with bids seen as 35 percent volatilities. May volatilities were still pricey at 36 percent.
Coffee options, mirroring the stable futures values, were generally quiet this week after some activity on Monday where 1,100 lots changed hands.
London's robusta futures were thinly-traded this week with May prices being kept at between $1,545 and $1,600 a tonne as the market tried to consolidate recent gains.
The market has so far shown little reaction to technically-inspired rally in New York arabica futures which revisited the highs of 192 cents a lb this week.
Analysts said London should clear the psychological $1,600 mark but needed more momentum to revisit last month's peaks above $1,800 a tonne.
In options, July volatilities had come off to around 40 percent from 42 percent a week earlier.

"The fall is surprising because July is a frost season," said one. "You won't be able to buy July at under 46 percent at this time last year but this year a lot of locals have discounted the chance of a frost."
"They are just taking the risk and offering the market down to 40 percent for July which historically is incredibly cheap," the trader added. One local was seen looking to buy July at 36 percent.
The last major frosts in 1994 wiped some Brazilian coffee trees and sent world prices soaring.
There is still no interest beyond July options and traders said September and November will start building up positions once May goes off the board on April 16.
"People are just squaring up May positions, selling out longs or going out of shorts. Suppose May coffee vols are irrelevant now," said one.
In cocoa options, market makers said there was a good interest in nearby options, buying July calls and selling May puts.
On Thursday, July 1,100 stg calls were traded 127 times.
May stole some activity ahead of its expiry this Wednesday. May 975 puts saw 300 lots traded at around 20 stg premium which at 36 percent volatilies were seen as quite expensive.
Cocoa futures took a sharp dive earlier this week to a low of 962 stg a tonne basis May on fund-led sell-off having risen to a high of 1,050 stg on April 2.

Although it has gradually recovered since, analysts said the market might still need to consolidate further before gathering fresh momentum towards the 1,020 area. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
